requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to contain at least 12 characters and at least three character classes.
requirements.summary: The effective configuration sets minlen=12, minclass=3, and all class credits to zero. PAM references pam_pwquality. Behavioral checks rejected an 11-character password and a 16-character two-class password while accepting a 20-character three-class password; the same configuration and behavior remained after reboot.

overall_summary: The requested password policy is satisfied and persisted across a verified restart. The restart protocol is coherent: node1 was running before restart, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity, returned to a running state, and retained working policy enforcement. Hygiene was good apart from two abandoned temporary files.
limitations: Password behavior was tested through pwscore with PAM integration inspected, but an end-to-end password change through passwd was not captured.
Package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.

The restart cross-check is complete and consistent: boot identity changed from a8e7c48c-f025-4f14-9fd0-ef6c37642e45 to c9df28ca-906c-4359-ab3e-d1b5333be68d in both executor and lifecycle evidence (cmd-45280e72cd99477d, cmd-70f6064a42704250, cmd-d01c2faf37d640cc, cmd-33f5706e8ce34679, global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity, global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity).

operational_hygiene.summary: The configuration edit and SELinux-context restoration were directly related to the task, and the reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were observed. Two low-risk temporary artifacts remained instead of being cleaned up: /tmp/pwquality.conf.pre-task, created by cmd-d05bbb413f234d06, and /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, created by cmd-70f6064a42704250. Both are confirmed as executor-created retained residue. No failed services or new listening endpoints were observed after execution.
